title: Who didn't notice?
setting: A weeknight at home. Okaasan has called Kenji down to dinner again and again, and has finally come up to his room. The curry is still simmering on the stove downstairs.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji! gohan dekita tte, nando mo itta noni. okaasan no koe, kikoenakatta?
lines.ja: ケンジ！ご飯できたって、何度も言ったのに。お母さんの声、聞こえなかった？
lines.kana: けんじ！ごはんできたって、なんどもいったのに。おかあさんのこえ、きこえなかった？
lines.english: Kenji! I've told you again and again that dinner's ready. Didn't you hear me?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e? gomen, ongaku kiitete, zenzen ki tsukanakatta.
lines.ja: え？ごめん、音楽聴いてて、全然気つかなかった。
lines.kana: え？ごめん、おんがくきいてて、ぜんぜんきつかなかった。
lines.english: Huh? Sorry, I had my music on. I didn't notice at all.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: mou. okaasan no hanashi, itsumo kikanai n da kara.
lines.ja: もう。お母さんの話、いつも聞かないんだから。
lines.kana: もう。おかあさんのはなし、いつもきかないんだから。
lines.english: Honestly. You never listen to a word I say.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: kiiteru yo! koe ga kikoenakatta dake da yo.
lines.ja: 聞いてるよ！声が聞こえなかっただけだよ。
lines.kana: きいてるよ！こえがきこえなかっただけだよ。
lines.english: I do listen! I just couldn't hear you.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: wakatta, wakatta. ii kara, sugu kite.
lines.ja: わかった、わかった。いいから、すぐ来て。
lines.kana: わかった、わかった。いいから、すぐきて。
lines.english: Okay, okay. Just come down now.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un. a, nanka ii nioi suru. kyou, karee?
lines.ja: うん。あ、なんかいい匂いする。今日、カレー？
lines.kana: うん。あ、なんかいいにおいする。きょう、かれー？
lines.english: Okay. Oh, something smells good. Is it curry tonight?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou. kenji no daisuki na karee.
lines.ja: そう。ケンジの大好きなカレー。
lines.kana: そう。けんじのだいすきなかれー。

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: yatta! are? ima, nanka oto shinakatta?
lines.ja: やった！あれ？今、なんか音しなかった？
lines.kana: やった！あれ？いま、なんかおとしなかった？
lines.english: Yes! Huh? Did you just hear something?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.english: A noise? I didn't hear anything.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shita yo, oto. e, nanka kogeta nioi mo shinai?
lines.ja: したよ、音。え、なんか焦げた匂いもしない？
lines.kana: したよ、おと。え、なんかこげたにおいもしない？
lines.english: There was a noise. Wait, can you smell something burning, too?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.english: Oh, you're right. Oh no, the curry!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: お母さん、危ない！気をつけて！
lines.kana: おかあさん、あぶない！きをつけて！

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: ああ、よかった。ちょっと焦げただけ。
lines.kana: ああ、よかった。ちょっとこげただけ。
lines.english: Phew, thank goodness. It's only a little burnt.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: okaasan mo, zenzen ki tsukanakatta ne.
lines.ja: お母さんも、全然気つかなかったね。
lines.kana: おかあさんも、ぜんぜんきつかなかったね。
lines.english: You didn't notice a thing either, Mum.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou ne. ki ga tsuite kurete, arigatou.
lines.ja: そうね。気がついてくれて、ありがとう。
lines.kana: そうね。きがついてくれて、ありがとう。

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: jaa, itadakimasu! un, chotto kogeta nioi suru kedo, saikou!
lines.ja: じゃあ、いただきます！うん、ちょっと焦げた匂いするけど、最高！
lines.kana: じゃあ、いただきます！うん、ちょっとこげたにおいするけど、さいこう！
lines.english: Right, let's eat! Mm, it smells a bit burnt, but it's great!

choices.english: Kenji was supposed to keep an eye on the curry but had his music on, and his mother is the one who smells it burning.
Kenji didn't hear his mother calling him to dinner. While she's telling him off, he hears a noise and smells burning: she'd left the curry on the stove. It's only a little burnt.
Kenji hears a noise and smells something burning, but his mother says it's nothing, and the curry burns so badly they can't eat it.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Okaasan told him again and again (nando mo itta noni), but he had music on and didn't notice (ongaku kiitete, zenzen ki tsukanakatta). Lines 8-10: Kenji hears a noise (oto shinakatta?) and then smells burning (kogeta nioi mo shinai?). Line 11: it's the curry, and line 13: it's only a little burnt (chotto kogeta dake). A is wrong: Kenji was up in his room, and he is the one who smells the burning (line 10); his mother hadn't noticed (line 14). C is wrong: she says there was no noise (line 9), but she agrees about the smell (line 11: honto da), and the curry is fine to eat: Kenji calls it saikou in line 16.

questions.english: You walk into the kitchen while Okaasan is cooking. She says "gohan, mou sugu dekiru yo." (Dinner's nearly ready.) Something smells great. Tell her.
questions.ja: ご飯、もうすぐできるよ。
questions.kana: ごはん、もうすぐできるよ。
questions.answer: Make the smell the subject and use suru, not kagu: a, ii nioi suru!

modelAnswers.ja: あ、なんかいい匂いする！

modelAnswers.romaji: un, ii nioi suru ne. kyou, karee?
modelAnswers.ja: うん、いい匂いするね。今日、カレー？
modelAnswers.english: Mm, that smells good. Is it curry tonight?

questions.explanation: Kenji says exactly this in line 6: a, nanka ii nioi suru. The smell is the subject and suru reports it; ga is usually dropped in casual speech. Don't reach for kagu (sniff): that's smelling on purpose, not a smell reaching you. Visiting someone like Satou-san, the polite version keeps ga: ii nioi ga shimasu ne.

questions.english: When Kenji first senses something is wrong, what does he ask his mother?
questions.ja: ケンジ君はお母さんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんじくんはおかあさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-kun wa okaasan ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Did you just listen to a noise? (kiku: listening on purpose)
Did you just hear something? (lit. 'wasn't there a noise?')

questions.explanation: Line 8: ima, nanka oto shinakatta? The noise is the subject and suru reports it: oto shita is 'there was a noise', here as a 'wasn't there...?' question, and his mother answers with the same verb (line 9: oto? shinakatta yo). A is the English 'did you hear a noise' built with kiku, but kiku is listening on purpose, like ongaku kiitete in line 2; for a sound that just reached you, natives say oto shita (or oto ga kikoeta). B is the smell version, but the smell comes later: in line 10 Kenji says kogeta nioi mo shinai?, with mo ('too') because it comes on top of the noise.

questions.english: Okaasan phones you, but the line is bad. She says "moshimoshi? are? moshimoshi?" Ask her if she can hear you.
questions.ja: もしもし？あれ？もしもし？
questions.kana: もしもし？あれ？もしもし？
questions.answer: Ask with kikoeru and your voice as the subject: moshimoshi, koe kikoeru? Not kiiteru? (are you listening?).

modelAnswers.ja: お母さん、声聞こえてる？

questions.explanation: On a call, the question is whether your voice is reaching her, so the verb is kikoeru with koe as the subject: koe kikoeru? or koe kikoeteru?. Okaasan asks the same thing in line 1 (okaasan no koe, kikoenakatta?). Don't say kiiteru?: that's 'are you listening?', and Kenji's comeback in line 4 turns on exactly this difference (kiiteru yo! koe ga kikoenakatta dake da yo: 'I do listen, I just couldn't hear you'). On a work call, make it polite: koe kikoemasu ka?

questions.english: In the kitchen, Kenji says to his mother "okaasan mo, zenzen ki tsukanakatta ne." What does he mean?

choices.english: She hadn't noticed the curry burning either, just as he hadn't noticed her calling.
She wasn't careful when she rushed down to the kitchen.
She doesn't listen to him either.

questions.explanation: Line 14: ki tsukanakatta is the past negative of ki ga tsuku, 'didn't notice', with ga dropped. The mo ('you too') points back to line 2, where Kenji said the same about not noticing her calling (zenzen ki tsukanakatta); now she hadn't noticed the burning smell. She takes the point in line 15: ki ga tsuite kurete, arigatou (thanks for noticing). B mixes it up with ki o tsukeru (be careful), which sounds almost the same: Kenji did shout ki o tsukete! as she ran downstairs (line 12), but that's a different phrase. C would be kikanai or kiitenakatta (not listening), which is her complaint about him in line 3, not his about her.

newWords.english: (not) at all (zenzen ki tsukanakatta = didn't notice at all)
something; kind of (nanka ii nioi suru = something smells good)
burn, get scorched (kogeta nioi = a burning smell)
